Description: Anchor links should scroll smoothly to target section
Do: Use scroll-behavior: smooth on html element

Description: Fixed nav should not obscure content
Do: Add padding-top to body equal to nav height
Don't: Let nav overlap first section content

Description: Current page/section should be visually indicated
Do: Highlight active nav item with color/underline
Don't: No visual feedback on current location

Description: Users expect back to work predictably
URLs should reflect current state for sharing
Show user location in site hierarchy
Do: Use for sites with 3+ levels of depth

Description: Too many animations cause distraction and motion sickness
Do: Animate 1-2 key elements per view maximum

Description: Animations should feel responsive not sluggish
Don't: Use animations longer than 500ms for UI

Description: Respect user's motion preferences
Show feedback during async operations
Don't: Leave UI frozen with no feedback

Description: Hover effects don't work on touch devices
Don't: Rely only on hover for important actions

Description: Infinite animations are distracting
Some CSS properties trigger expensive repaints
Do: Use transform and opacity for animations

Description: Linear motion feels robotic
Do: Use ease-out for entering ease-in for exiting

Description: Stacking context conflicts cause hidden elements
Hidden overflow can clip important content
Do: Test all content fits within containers

Description: Fixed elements can overlap or be inaccessible
Do: Account for safe areas and other fixed elements
Code Example Good: Fixed nav + fixed bottom with gap

Description: New stacking contexts reset z-index
Do: Understand what creates new stacking context
Don't: Expect z-index to work across contexts

Description: Layout shift when content loads is jarring
100vh can be problematic on mobile browsers
Do: Use dvh or account for mobile browser chrome

Description: Content too wide is hard to read
Don't: Let text span full viewport width

Description: Small buttons are hard to tap accurately
Adjacent touch targets need adequate spacing
Custom gestures can conflict with system
Do: Avoid horizontal swipe on main content

Description: 300ms tap delay feels laggy
Accidental refresh is frustrating
Tactile feedback improves interaction feel
Do: Use for confirmations and important actions

Description: Keyboard users need visible focus indicators
Do: Use visible focus rings on interactive elements

Description: Visual feedback on interactive elements
Do: Change cursor and add subtle visual change
Don't: No hover feedback on clickable elements

Description: Show immediate feedback on press/click
Clearly indicate non-interactive elements
Prevent double submission during async actions
Do: Disable button and show loading state

Description: Users need to know when something fails
Do: Show clear error messages near problem

Description: Confirm successful actions to users
Do: Show success message or visual change

Description: Prevent accidental destructive actions
Text must be readable against background
Don't convey information by color alone
Do: Use icons/text in addition to color

Description: Images need text alternatives
Do: Descriptive alt text for meaningful images

Description: Screen readers use headings for navigation
Don't: Skip heading levels or misuse for styling

Description: Interactive elements need accessible names
All functionality accessible via keyboard
Don't: Keyboard traps or illogical tab order

Description: Content should make sense when read aloud
Do: Use semantic HTML and ARIA properly

Description: Inputs must have associated labels
Do: Use label with for attribute or wrap input

Description: Error messages must be announced
Do: Use aria-live or role=alert for errors

Description: Allow keyboard users to skip navigation
Do: Provide skip to main content link
Don't: No skip link on nav-heavy pages

Description: Large images slow page load
Load content as needed
Do: Lazy load below-fold images and content

Description: Large bundles slow initial load
Repeat visits should be fast
Web fonts can block rendering
External scripts can block rendering
Large JavaScript slows interaction
CSS/JS can block first paint
Every input needs a visible label
Do: Always show label above or beside input

Description: Errors should appear near the problem
Don't: Single error message at top of form

Description: Validate as user types or on blur
Do: Validate on blur for most fields

Description: Use appropriate input types
Do: Use email tel number url etc

Description: Help browsers autofill correctly
Mark required fields clearly
Let users see password while typing
Confirm form submission status
Inputs should look interactive
Don't: Inputs that look like plain text

Description: Show appropriate keyboard for input type
Design for mobile then enhance for larger
Do: Start with mobile styles then add breakpoints

Description: Test at all common screen sizes
Mobile layouts need touch-sized targets
Text must be readable on all devices
Set viewport for mobile devices
Avoid horizontal scrolling
Images should scale with container
Tables can overflow on mobile
Do: Use horizontal scroll or card layout

Description: Adequate line height improves readability
Long lines are hard to read
Consistent type hierarchy aids scanning
Fonts should load without layout shift
Body text needs good contrast
Do: Use darker text on light backgrounds

Description: Headings should stand out from body
Show system status during waits
Guide users when no content exists
Help users recover from errors
Show progress for multi-step processes
Transient messages for non-critical info
Confirm successful actions
Handle long content gracefully
Do: Truncate with ellipsis and expand option

Description: Use locale-appropriate date formats
Format large numbers for readability
Show realistic placeholders during dev
Users should be able to skip tutorials
Help users find results faster
Dead ends frustrate users
Editing one by one is tedious
Users need to know they talk to AI
Waiting for full text is slow
Do: Stream text response token by token

Description: Elements should respond to eye tracking before pinch
UI needs Z-depth to separate content from environment
Video consumes massive data and energy
Heavy 3D/Image assets increase carbon footprint
AI needs user feedback to improve
Parallax/Scroll-jacking causes nausea
AI-generated UIs converge on the same default look (purple gradients, Inter, generic centered heroes) which erodes differentiation
Do: Deliberately vary typography, palette, and layout from the default AI look
Don't: Default to purple-gradient + Inter + centered hero
Code Example Good: font-family: 'Space Grotesk' with a custom palette

Description: Pre-selecting the most common choice for every field reduces decision fatigue; 70-90% of users never change defaults so a default reads as a recommendation
Do: Pre-fill fields with the most common option and let users scan and adjust
Don't: Present blank forms that stack decisions on the user

Description: The closer people feel to finishing the faster they move; you choose where the starting line is
Do: Pre-fill progress indicators (2 of 10 stamps) so completion feels near
Don't: Never show 0% complete when the real work is minimal

Description: Giving something first (free report sample or tool) creates a pull to return the favor
Do: Provide free value before asking for signup or purchase
Don't: Ask for commitment with nothing given first
Code Example Bad: Signup wall with no free value

Description: The first number a user sees sets the anchor for every later comparison
Do: Sequence prices and options so the reference point works for you
Don't: Let ranges or high numbers anchor perception by accident
Code Example Good: Show reference price before discounted price

Description: People value what they build themselves more than identical ready-made items
Do: Let users create choose or customize before asking for commitment
Don't: Present a finished product with no user input

Description: Just feeling ownership is enough to make closing the tab costly
Do: Give the user something that belongs to them on the signup screen
Don't: Offer nothing the user would lose by leaving

Description: Bottom nav is prime real estate; more tabs shrink tap targets and induce choice paralysis
Do: Keep 3-5 tabs (max 6) covering only top-level frequently used destinations
Don't: Expose 7+ tabs to show everything at once
Code Example Good: 5 tabs: Home Search Create Messages Profile

Description: The center of the bottom nav is the most prominent and thumb-reachable position on large phones
Do: Place one high-value action (create post order) in the center styled to stand out
Don't: Treat the primary action as just another tab with equal weight
Code Example Bad: Primary action as a plain tab

Description: A single cue (text-only or color-only) is too subtle; users lose orientation
Do: Signal the active state with at least two visual changes (outline-to-filled icon plus color)
Don't: Rely on one weak signal like slightly darker text
Code Example Good: Icon fill + color change on active tab
Code Example Bad: Darker text only on active tab

Description: Equal-opacity nav icons make the current screen unreadable at a glance
Do: Render the active tab at full strength and inactive tabs visibly muted (~60% opacity)
Don't: Keep equal opacity across all nav icons
Code Example Good: Active icon full opacity inactives at 60%

Description: Color-only active states fail for colorblind and low-vision users
Do: Signal the current tab with shape or elevation plus a color flip
Don't: Identify the active tab by hue alone
Code Example Good: Recessed pill shape + accent fill on active tab
Code Example Bad: Active tab differs only by color

Description: Without a clear active marker users can't tell where they are in a carousel
Do: Pair every carousel or selector with a visible active-state indicator that relocates with selection
Don't: Imply selection by the item merely being centered
Code Example Good: Colored underline bar that moves with the active item

Description: Dense flat link lists are hard to scan and click
Do: Group footer links into labeled columns with darker group titles and lighter list items
Don't: Ship a single undifferentiated block of footer links
Code Example Good: Labeled footer columns with title/item color contrast
Code Example Bad: One flat list of footer links

Description: Most phones are used one-handed; actions at the top force stretching or grip changes
Do: Position key buttons and navigation in the lower thumb-reachable region
Don't: Park the most-used action outside the natural thumb arc
Code Example Good: Primary CTA in bottom action bar
Code Example Bad: Primary CTA at top of screen

Description: A fixed bottom bar that overlaps content or the home indicator feels broken
Do: Reserve the nav height in the layout from the start and leave ~34px above the home indicator
Don't: Let long content run beneath a fixed bottom bar

Description: 'Subscribe' reads as recurring locked-in commitment; light verbs imply beginnings
Do: Use 'Start my free trial' with concrete friction reducers ('start in two taps')

Description: Hiding the total and cancellation terms feeds hidden-fee and change-of-plan anxiety
Do: State the all-in total and the cancellation window next to the CTA
Don't: Defer cost and policy questions to the next screen

Description: Equal-looking options make users default to the lowest-risk choice
Do: Design choice as visually weighted cards with the desired option pre-selected and tagged
Don't: Present two options as visually equal
Code Example Good: Pre-checked subscribe card with 'most popular' tag

Description: Interaction cost compounds for new users; banners add a tap between user and value
Do: Surface a curated relevant feed as the first screen and skip interstitial prompts
Don't: Hide content behind banners that demand an extra action

Description: Users can't commit to something they can't visualize; real product imagery does the convincing
Do: Feature genuine product content (real pages screens results) in marketing imagery
Don't: Show only an isolated product shot with no peek inside
Code Example Good: Product in consumption context with real screens

Description: Text placed over photos often fails contrast and hurts readability
Do: Darken the photo region behind text with a subtle gradient so copy clears WCAG contrast
Don't: Sit body text on mid-tone image areas with no scrim
Code Example Good: Linear gradient scrim behind overlay text

Description: Placeholder styled as strongly as typed values makes an empty field look pre-filled
Do: Render search hints at reduced opacity until the user types
Don't: Weight and color the placeholder identically to real input
Code Example Bad: Placeholder same weight as input value

Description: A bare empty state is a lost opportunity; it dead-ends and abandons users
Do: State the value add an illustration list 1-2 next actions and include a create CTA
Don't: Ship empty screens with no direction or call to action
Code Example Good: No projects yet + Create first project CTA
Code Example Bad: No items message with nothing else

Description: Launch time is wasted on a bare screen
Do: Show the app name plus one catchy value line on the loading frame
Don't: Leave a plain empty or purely decorative launch frame

Description: Ranges become max-cost anchors and force multi-option mental negotiation
Do: Show one firm price per option so options compare in seconds
Don't: Present ranges thinking they are more honest

Description: A bare price has no reference point and feels like a plain cost
Do: Pair the price with a clear crossed-out original anchor and visible savings
Don't: Let anchoring work against you via ranges
